name: MedBullets
intro: MedBullets是与JAMA Clinical Challenge并列但独立统计的医学问答数据集，含308道2022年4月至2023年12月公开的Step 2/3模拟临床题。论文移除图像而非宣称剔除图像依赖病例；官方数据中仍有116题正文出现“Figure”。每题保留病例、五个选项、答案及覆盖各选项的医疗专业人士解析，并另有四选项版本。
build_method: 公开网页采集, 图像移除, 专家解析保留, 四/五选项版本
metric: Accuracy, ROUGE-L, BERTScore, BLEURT, BARTScore+, BARTScore++, CTC, G-Eval
openness: 数据公开；仓库及数据无许可证文件
eval_feature: 答案与解释分别评测, 三种提示策略, 自动与人工解释评估
openness_en: Public data; repository and dataset have no license file
build_method_en: Public-web collection, image removal, retained expert explanations, four/five-choice variants
eval_feature_en: Separate answer and explanation evaluation, three prompting strategies, automatic and human rationale assessment
intro_en: MedBullets is a medical QA dataset introduced alongside but counted separately from JAMA Clinical Challenge. It contains 308 public Step 2/3 simulated clinical questions posted from April 2022 through December 2023. The paper removes images; it does not claim to exclude image-dependent cases, and 116 released questions still contain the literal word ‘Figure’. Each item preserves a case, five choices, the answer, and a medical-professional explanation covering the options, with a separate four-choice variant.

drawio_review_note: Primary-source audit pinned the paper to arXiv:2402.18060v6 (last revised 2026-02-18; PDF SHA-256 e3fb199ebd1e9437194234bbe7ff9e81f0aca4c373ab2787c37ba5446e15d552), the official HanjieChen/ChallengeClinicalQA repository to HEAD 013b9447f2a2426155c0de02a42e03d4540a3501, and the Medbullets data to its last modifying commit d20bfca3cff061460fc216e85899a86e52da4934. The pinned repository contains no license file, no Medbullets collection script, and no inference, parser, or evaluation implementation; it releases only the fixed Medbullets CSV/JSON snapshots plus JAMA URLs/scrapers. Direct inspection verified 308 non-empty records in each medbullets_op5 and medbullets_op4 JSON, identical link sets, identical question and explanation text, and the same correct answer text for all 308 pairs. Every four-choice row removes exactly one wrong five-choice option, but the remaining released choice order differs for 244 of 308 items; neither the variant-generation code nor RNG seed is published. The five-choice and four-choice JSON SHA-256 values are 14e209d0dc5c6350290e878b8e7e392c976cc96765b8e2d0d7434a2787ea6998 and 1e1581c1b8d2f79735e71b8d07d0210a829087aac18e078dadc2ec2cb42ed68b. Paper Section 2 and Appendix A say links to open-access Step 2/3 questions were collected from Medbullets posts on X from April 2022 through December 2023, pages were crawled, images were filtered out, text was retained, and source explanations were written by doctors or other medical professionals. They do not say that image-dependent cases were excluded: 116 of 308 pinned question strings still contain the literal word ‘Figure’, so the previous exclusion claim was removed and the unresolved image dependency is explicit. JAMA Clinical Challenge remains a separate 1,524-item, 13-domain companion track and is not counted in the 308; licensing prevents its raw public release. Appendix A's random choice-order study evaluates Medbullets-5 and JAMA, while TS-Guessing evaluates Medbullets-5, JAMA, and MedQA-4; both studies are diagnostic only and remove no items. Sections 3-4 and Appendix B.1 preserve seven exact model aliases; GPT-3.5/4 use T=1 and top-p=1; Llama 2 uses T=.8, top-p=.95, repetition penalty 1.1, and max 1,024 tokens; Llama 3 uses T=.85 and top-p=.95; PaLM 2 uses T=.8; MedAlpaca uses fp16, max 512 tokens, repetition penalty 1.1, and beam size 2; Meerkat uses fp16 greedy decoding, max 1,024 tokens, T=.7, and repetition penalty 1.0; all reported results use one run per model setting. The paper evaluates model-specific X-to-Y, two-stage X-to-R-to-Y, and gold-conditioned XY*-to-R prompts, plus zero/two/five-shot direct prompting with random leave-one-out demonstrations. Answer scoring is paper-level Accuracy against gold; no official parser, malformed/multiple/no-answer rule, or executable denominator contract is released. Explanation scoring includes ROUGE-L, BERTScore, BLEURT, BARTScore+/++, three CTC axes, and three G-Eval axes; Appendix B.3 uses GPT-4o at temperature 1, maximum five tokens, and averages five G-Eval runs, while package/checkpoint versions and failures remain unpinned. The separate human study samples 30 Medbullets-5 items, evaluates GPT-4 and PaLM 2 explanations with US Medicine/Healthcare Master's- or Doctoral-degree raters, scores completeness through per-choice checkboxes and correctness/relevance on 1-5 Likert scales, collects three ratings per output, filters unusually fast annotations, averages remaining scores per property, and reports Bennett S of 0.60 for correctness and 0.65 for relevance; completeness agreement is not computed. The paper reports answer and explanation findings separately and defines no single composite benchmark score. Formal publication evidence [site-a11s-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 4125×921 (English) and 4125×921 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 4123×919 and 4123×919. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
